description: The investigators go to the noble mansion, trace history through family portraits, roll Spot Hidden, and discover the family's deep connection to an ancient curse.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Gem Garden is a terraced garden. The sign at the entrance indicates it contains antiques from Trieste and Aquileia. Normally, this is a charming place where one could spend a lazy afternoon, but today the cold wind howls between the statues and pillars, and the garden is deserted. On the slope, there is a replica of a Roman Temple, currently hidden under the bending Plane Tree swaying in the cold wind. This is also the only spot in the garden offering shelter from the wind.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Crossing arms

conversation.speaker: player5

conversation.speaker: player6

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Gem Garden extends downward in steps, with each terrace displaying marble fragments from different eras: broken Corinthian capitals slanting into the frozen soil, mottled epitaph slabs arranged in a semicircle along rusty iron railings. The wind continues to sweep across the terraces, rattling the hinges of the information signs.

conversation.text: Inside the case, black walnut wood boxes lined with faded crimson velvet are laid flat, the cloth sunken into seven circular depressions. The first row holds four medals arranged left to right: the first depicts the outline of the Trojan Horse, its hooves sinking into greenish patina; the second shows Alexander astride Bucephalus, the spear tip blackened by oxidation; the third portrays Cleopatra's wrist holding the asp, the snake scales and hair strands filled with dust; the fourth displays the folds of Caesar's toga at his assassination, the details of the Senate steps blurred. The three medals in the second row are slightly misaligned: the leftmost shows Hannibal's elephants crossing the Alps, with fine cracks on the ivory surfaces; the middle medal captures the moment Spartacus swings his sword, the blade and chains connected by rust; the last depicts Odysseus bound to the mast to escape the sirens, the etching lines of the sail covered in verdigris. The backs of all medals are pressed against the velvet, their edges fitting snugly into the depressions.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: As Bolan approaches the sarcophagus, she notices the relief band extending from the edge of the lid. The group of sacrificial human statues is severely worn: the figure on the far left holding the offering tray is missing its entire right arm, the break covered with a grayish-white calcified layer; the face of the kneeling figure in the middle is eroded into a blurred pit; the clothing folds of the figures on the right have melted into wavy protrusions. In sharp contrast are the reptile group receiving the sacrifices. Seven dragon-like creatures are coiled in the upper right corner of the relief, each scale carved with dense radial patterns, their claws deeply embedded in the stone material forming sharp shadows. The head of the leading creature is abnormally large, its snout occupying two-thirds of the head length, the eye sockets are two perfectly spherical depressions drilled out. The tails of all creatures intertwine into a spiral structure, with no signs of weathering visible in any scale crevice. The junction of the reliefs forms a bizarre visual split—the human part glows with the yellowish patina common in museums, while the reptile area displays the bluish-gray hue characteristic of fresh limestone, as if carved just yesterday.

The posture of these creatures reminds her of pagan rituals preserved in volcanic ash in Pompeii murals, but Roman art never featured dragon-like creatures with such distorted head proportions—the snout length completely violates the skull structure of any reptile recorded in natural history.

conversation.text: An elderly man in a dark gray three-piece suit, leaning on a black ebony cane, walks in quickly and pauses upon seeing Bolan. Ah, you must be Professor Bolan from Miskatonic University? I saw your photo on the cover of last year's archaeology journal. He pulls out a slightly creased business card from his pocket and hands it over. I'm Ernesto Pabeno, the curator here. I truly didn't expect you to visit our little place.

conversation.speaker: player2

In 1910, we purchased them from the descendants of Marcus Termona. He pulls a pen from his breast pocket and writes something on a small notepad. His father Marcus was a famous local collector last century; now his son has inherited the estate and does academic research. If you're interested in Winkelmann's relics, visiting him might be helpful. "The curator hands Bolan a page torn from the notepad, with scribbled handwriting: Antonio Termona, Corso Vittorio 17.

conversation.text: The investigators walked along the Bora-howling Cathedral Street and finally pushed open the wooden door of a restaurant with a copper bell. They chose a seat by the window. The window glass was fogged with condensation from the temperature difference, faintly revealing moving figures outside. The stray cat emerged from player4's coat and quietly crouched beside the radiator under the table.

Glass display cases contained ivory chess sets and several Renaissance medals. A landscape oil painting hung above the fireplace, and the coffee table held the day's Trieste newspaper.
